youtube.title: Alexis St. Martin: The Man With a Hole Into His Stomach
youtube.description:
Alexis St. Martin had a hole into his stomach, and a doctor lowered food into it on a silk string. In 1822 a musket went off by accident in a fur trading store on Mackinac Island and hit the young voyageur at close range.

Army surgeon William Beaumont saved his life, but the wound healed into a permanent opening. Over about 200 experiments, Beaumont showed that digestion is chemical: gastric juice is acid, and it dissolves food instead of grinding it. His book came out in 1833. St. Martin hated being a test subject and fled home to Canada more than once.

Subscribe to Stickstory for a true story like this every day. Would you have let a doctor study you like that? Tell me in the comments!

scenes.text: This man had a hole in his stomach.
scenes.visual: Hook frame in a plain 1820s room: young St. Martin stands big on the left, side-on, blue cap, uneasy face, shirt hanging open; on his left side under the ribs a round gauze pad with a small dark round opening into his stomach, a red ring pulsing round it on 'hole'; the fez host stands big on the right in shock (wide eyes, open mouth), arm stretched out, a silk string running from his hand to a chunk of meat that hangs just above the hole.

Mackinac Island from the shore: Fort Mackinac's white walls, blockhouse and waving flag on a green bluff to the right, the fur company's log store with a smoking chimney on the left; on 'musket' a big gold muzzle flash bursts from the store door and a cloud of smoke rolls out; hand label 'MACKINAC ISLAND' and red box '1822'.

scenes.text: and hit fur trader Alexis St. Martin.
scenes.visual: Inside the fur company store: shelves of fur bundles and striped blanket stacks, a long counter with a musket on it that flashes and smokes; fur trader St. Martin (blue cap) is knocked back in shock on 'hit', smoke drifting past him; a keg and a crate in front; red box 'ALEXIS ST. MARTIN'.

scenes.text: William Beaumont saved him, but the wound never closed.
scenes.visual: A doctor's room: bottle shelf, framed certificate, a hanging oil lamp; St. Martin sits with a bandage on his side while Dr. Beaumont stands and points at it; on 'closed' a small round dark window opens in the bandage, a red ring pulses round it, red box 'STILL OPEN' with an arrow; front table with a doctor's bag, a bowl and a flickering candle.

scenes.text: So he tied food to a silk string,
scenes.visual: Close-up of St. Martin's healed side: the open shirt hangs on both sides of a round gauze pad round a small round opening, the shirt hem and trousers at the bottom; a hand in a blue army-coat cuff with gold buttons holds a hanging silk string above it; a chunk of meat, a piece of bread and a cabbage leaf pop onto the string one under the other; hand label 'silk string' with an arrow.

scenes.text: dropped it in, and pulled it out hours later.
scenes.visual: A cut-away of the body side: the skin line on the left, ribs at the top, a big J-shaped stomach with folds and the short tunnel through the wall; on 'dropped' the string slides the meat, bread and leaf through the tunnel into the stomach; on 'hours' the hands of a clock spin round; on 'pulled' the food comes back out, much smaller.

scenes.text: It wasn't ground up. Acid dissolved it.
scenes.visual: The same cut-away: on 'ground' a pair of turning millstones beside the stomach gets a big red X; then gold gastric juice pools in the stomach, drops run down the wall and bubbles fizz while the food shrinks away; red box 'ACID'.

scenes.text: St. Martin hated being a test subject and fled to Canada.
scenes.visual: On the beach by the fur company store: St. Martin sits in a birch-bark canoe on the water with a paddle, a small round patch at his side, angry; on 'Canada' the canoe slides off to the right; Dr. Beaumont is left on the sand holding his notes, worried, then reaches after him; hand label 'to Canada' with an arrow.

scenes.text: But that hole taught the world how your stomach works.
scenes.visual: Top view of a desk: Beaumont's 1833 book lies open, a page turns, the left page reads 'GASTRIC JUICE' and '1833', on the right page a stomach sketch with a string draws itself; quill and inkwell, spectacles and a candle around it; gold rings spread out from the book on 'world' (that hole taught the world).

scenes.text: Subscribe for a true story like this every day.
scenes.visual: The beach below the fort: the fez host stands big and waves, then points at the viewer; the canoe rests on the sand, Fort Mackinac's flag waves on the bluff.
